audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Jax level 1 at 8/10 while whys[0] says neither champion can commit, gives Skill at 4-5 and first item while whys[3] and whys[5] describe Jax owning both, and gives Jax the 2+ items row while whys[6], spikes[3] and late all say Yasuo out-scales hard.
audit.why: The packet chart (Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Yasuo) matches the prose and the 55.14% win rate over 2198 games: Jax owns levels 2 through first item on Counter Strike, and loses the two-item duel to Infinity Edge and Shieldbow.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Yasuo across both layers as one atomic group, ratings adjusted, and phases[6].why rewritten so the last row no longer claims Jax's pattern is at full power.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is written "Grandmaster at Arms" in whys[4], spikes[2].text and mid.
audit.why: The ability is Grandmaster's Might, 110/100/90s. phases[4].why already uses the correct name on the same page.
audit.corrected: Renamed in all three. Spike order otherwise verified: Jax at 2, 3 and 6; Yasuo at two items where crit items arrive.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction — Wind Wall being useless against Leap Strike — is stated but never given the cooldown that makes it exploitable, and Last Breath is described only as 'his all-in after a knockup' with no timer.
audit.why: Wind Wall blocks projectiles for 4 seconds on a 25s cooldown at rank 1; Leap Strike is a targeted dash with no projectile, so the wall does nothing to your engage and he cannot save it for you. Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 dropping to 30s at rank 3, and it requires an airborne target — so his Q3 tornado is the real trigger to deny, and the gap you fight in shrinks badly as he ranks R.
audit.corrected: whys[3] now carries Wind Wall's 25s and Counter Strike's rank-3 13s; dosFull[0].d names Last Breath's 70s and its knockup requirement.

edits.after: Two items in, Infinity Edge and Shieldbow let him eat your stun and keep critting. End the game before that timing lands.

edits.before: His all-in after a knockup. While down, you win. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It needs a knockup and it is 70s at rank 1 — fight in that gap, and deny the tornado.

edits.before: Your dodge-stun comes up more often as you rank Counter Strike, and his Wind Wall does nothing against your targeted, projectile-less Q.
edits.after: Counter Strike drops to 13s by rank 3, and his 25s Wind Wall blocks projectiles only — your targeted Leap Strike walks straight through it.

edits.after: Grandmaster's Might — your hardest all-in. The instant Armor/MR steroid soaks his crit burst while your every-third on-hit and E-stun grind him out before he can land an airborne R.

edits.before: This is your stretch. Counter Strike hard-counters his entire damage pattern: his crit autos get dodged and his tornado windup gets stunned out of, so every time he commits he loses the trade. At 6 your Grandmaster at Arms is the dagger — the instant Armor and MR soaks whatever crit lands while your every-third on-hit grinds him down, so E-stun into R is a clean kill before he can find an airborne target for his own R. Watch his E dash through the minion wave: that's how he resets spacing and slips your Leap Strike, so wait until he's spent his dash or is on your side of the wave before you all-in.
edits.after: This is your stretch. Counter Strike hard-counters his entire damage pattern: Steel Tempest is treated as a basic attack, so the dodge eats his Q as well as his crits, and the tornado windup gets stunned out of. At 6 Grandmaster's Might is the dagger — the instant Armor and MR soaks whatever crit lands while your every-third on-hit grinds him down, so E-stun into R is a clean kill before he finds an airborne target for his own 70s R. Watch his E dash through the minion wave: on a 0.5s cooldown he resets spacing at will, so all-in only when he is on your side of the wave.

notes: The page already gets the Wind Wall interaction right — Leap Strike is a targeted dash with no projectile, so the wall does not stop it — and I added the 25s cooldown behind that claim rather than changing it. Sweeping Blade's 0.5s cooldown is now on the page in mid, which is the number that explains why he can always reposition out of a leap. Left unverified: the claim in late and spikes[3] that his crit 'punches through your stun' with Shieldbow — the item behaviour is not in the kits, so I kept the existing wording and did not extend it.
